text: Cause is of three kinds, based on the distinction between inherent, non-inherent, and instrumental causes. That in which the effect is inherently present is the inherent cause; for example, the threads are the inherent cause of the cloth, and the cloth is the inherent cause of its own form and other attributes. When a cause is conjoined with the effect or another cause in a single entity, that cause is the non-inherent cause; for example, the conjunction of threads is the non-inherent cause of the cloth, and the form of the threads is the non-inherent cause of the form of the cloth. A cause that is distinct from both of these is the instrumental cause; for example, the loom and similar tools are the instrumental causes of the cloth. Among these three types of causes, that cause which is unique is called the instrument. || 37 ||
